 Rajasthan High Court says delayed tax refunds carry statutory interest, sets 30 day timeline
 Rajasthan High Court says a department that delays a due tax refund must pay statutory interest under Section 56 of the Sales Tax Act.
 Ekta Sharma Published: October 24, 2026, 9:56 pm 
 Share Home » Rajasthan High Court » Raj HC Jodhpur » Rajasthan High Court says delayed tax refunds carry statutory interest, sets 30 day timeline 
 The division bench of justice Arun Monga and Justice Yogendra Kumar Purohit
 Jodhpur: The Rajasthan High Court has said the tax department must pay interest if its delay holds up a refund that is due. A division bench was hearing a company’s plea for return of a pre-deposit of about Rs 1.05 cr paid to file tax appeals.
 Justice Arun Monga and Justice Yogendra Kumar Purohit disposed of the petition of a Jodhpur pan masala maker.
 The company was taxed under the Rajasthan Tax on Luxuries (Tobacco and its Products) Act, 1994, which the High Court struck down in 2005. Assessment orders in 2006 still raised demands of about Rs 6.83 cr and Rs 5.61 cr for two years, on the ground that it had recovered the tax from customers.

 Follow on Google News Add as preferred source The company made the pre-deposit and won its appeals in 2010. The refund was never paid. After years of representations, it asked the High Court for the money with 12 per cent interest.
 The State said the writ was not maintainable. It said it had appealed to the Rajasthan Tax Board. The Commissioner had withheld the refund, citing Section 54 of the Rajasthan Value Added Tax Act, because releasing it could hurt revenue.
 The Bench pointed to Section 56 of the Rajasthan Sales Tax Act, 1994. At first sight, it said, the provision creates a statutory duty to pay interest where the department’s delay holds up a refund that is due.
 It cited a Division Bench ruling in Kwality Conduit Pvt Ltd v Commercial Taxes Officer , which said:
 “…once the statutory provision binds the respondents to pay interest on the refunded amount, there is no way the respondents could escape this statutory obligation.”
 Counsel for the State fairly agreed that the company could file a representation with its calculations. The Court directed it to do so within 15 days of the order being uploaded. The department must decide it within 30 days after that.
 The Bench clarified that the direction is only to verify the calculations. If they are in order, they must be accepted. Otherwise, interest is payable under Section 56. The order does not record a finding on the State’s plea that the refund could be withheld while its appeal is pending.
